newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Negara checks ringgit rate at 2.57 dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara checks ringgit rate at 2.57 dlr.

text.p: The central Bank Negara Malaysia checked dollar/ringgit rates at 2.57 in late-afternoon Kuala Lumpur trading, dealers said.
The rate-checking was done through its agent banks in the capital city as the ringgit was threatening to fall below that level against the dollar, they said.
"They were checking but there was no offers," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
"They were just hanging around there to inform people that they are watching,' said another dealer.
But some dealers said they heard that Bank Negara had actually intervened by selling a "small amount" of dollars for ringgit.
No confirmation was available from the central bank. It does not normally comment on its open market operations.
Bank Negara had intervened to block the fall of the ringgit at 2.57 a dollar on Monday in New York trading.
One dealer at a large Malaysian bank, who heard Bank Negara had intervened, said the central bank appeared as the ringgit was sold down due to sales out of London.
"London was paying (2.5700/10). Right now there are still offers at (2.5790/00)," the dealer said.
Dealers said the rise in dollar/ringgit could have been fuelled by stops placed just behind 2.5660 after the market was confined to the 2.5590-2.5660 range throughout the day.
They said rate movements were exaggerated by thin trading ahead of a holiday in Malaysia on Thursday.
Dealers expect the dollar to test higher levels during London trading.
They said the ringgit's undertone remains bearish due to a perceived change in stance by Malaysian authorities.

Acting Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday that Malaysia would allow the exchange rate to be determined by market forces and that the country did not favour a high interest rate regime.
Anwar's comments baffled the market after Bank Negara governor Ahmad Mohamed Don said last week that interest rates would stay high to curb speculation in the ringgit, dealers said.

The statement was also interpreted that the authorities were willing to tolerate further ringgit weakness, dealers said, adding that they did not discount the possibility of funds pushing dollar/ringgit towards 2.60.
At 0930 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5720/50 to a dollar. It closed at 2.5580/10 in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
